# Mara Voss

A photographic survey of high altitude and quiet lowland, collected across the last eight years.
Everything below renders in any markdown preview; the directives carry structure for the portfolio
site and its CMS.

---

## The work

My practice sits where weather meets geology. I shoot on large format in the mountains and on a
handheld camera in the valleys, chasing the hour when light stops describing the land and starts
owning it.

> Selection is an edit, not a record. What you see here is roughly one frame kept for every six
> hundred taken.

## Field notes

Each trip begins with weeks of map reading and ends with days of waiting. The camera is the least
of it — the useful skill is knowing when the cloud will lift, and trusting that moment when it
does. I return to the same ridge for years before I consider a subject mine.

<!-- col -->
**At a glance**

- Prints: 40 × 60 cm, archival
- Format: 4×5 and 35 mm
- Editions: 12, signed
<!-- /columns -->

## The lowlands

Not every landscape needs a summit. The floodplain work is quieter and harder to sell, and I am
fondest of it for that reason. Reeds, fog, the slow geometry of drained fields.

<!-- media class="hero" -->
![Marsh at dawn](images/marsh.svg)

## Commissioning

A private portfolio review is available for curators, editors, and gallery owners. Prints travel
well; the negatives do not, so most conversations begin with the files and end with a visit.
